summary: fix(e-boekhouden): tighten cache directory/file permissions and re-chmod on rewrite
reason: This CLI was printed at generator v4.22.0, before the cache-permission hardening in cli-printing-press (commit ae1f46baf, 2026-07-20) landed upstream. writeCache used 0o755/0o644 (world-readable), exposing cached invoice/relation/ledger/mutation responses to other local users on a shared machine. Separately, os.WriteFile's perm argument only applies when creating a file, so even after tightening the mode, an existing cache file written under the old 0o644 code stayed world-readable across an upgrade until manually deleted.
validated_outcome: go build ./... and go test ./... pass. Added TestWriteCache_RechmodsExistingFile, confirmed to fail without the fix (asserts 0o644 stays 0o644) and pass with it. Greptile review threads on PR #1867 resolved for both the initial permission finding and the existing-file re-chmod finding.

deferred_to_upstream.feature: writeCacheWithHeaders (internal/generator/templates/client.go.tmpl) should chmod the cache file after every write, not only the cache directory after MkdirAll
deferred_to_upstream.reason: The rewrite-time re-chmod gap exists in the current generator template too, not only in this stale print -- any printed CLI upgrading past an older, laxer-permission generator version keeps serving pre-existing cache files at the old mode indefinitely until the cache is cleared.
